segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Hello. Do you mind if I ask you some questions about your journey today? We’re doing a customer satisfaction survey.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes. OK. I’ve got about ten minutes before my train home leaves. I’m on a day trip.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Great. Thank you. So first of all, could you tell me your name?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: It’s Sophie Bird.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Thank you. And would you mind telling me what you do?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: I’m a journalist. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh really? That must be interesting.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes. It is.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: So was the reason for your visit here today work?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Actually, it’s my day off. I came here to do some shopping. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: On right.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: But I do sometimes come here for work.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. Now I’d like to ask some questions about your journey today, if that’s OK.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes. No problem.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right, so can you tell me which station you’re travelling back to?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Staunfirth [[ ]] , where I live.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Can I just check the spelling? S-T-A-U-N-F-I-R-T-H?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: That’s right.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And you travelled from there this morning?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK, good. Next, can I ask what kind of ticket you bought? I assume it wasn’t a season ticket, as you don’t travel every day.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: That’s right. No, I just got a normal return [[ ]] ticket. I don’t have a rail card so I didn’t get any discount. I keep meaning to get one because it’s a lot cheaper.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes – you’d have saved 20% on your ticket today. So you paid the full price for your ticket?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. Do you think that’s good value for money?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Not really. I think it’s too much for a journey that only takes 45 minutes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, that’s one of the main complaints we get. So, you didn’t buy your ticket in advance?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: No. I know it’s cheaper if you buy a week in advance but I didn’t know I was coming then.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I know. You can’t always plan ahead. So, did you buy it this morning?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: No, it was yesterday.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right. And do you usually buy your tickets at the station?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Well, I do usually but the ticket office closes early and I hate using ticket machines. I think ticket offices should be open for longer hours. There’s always a queue for the machines and they’re often out of order.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: A lot of customers are saying the same thing.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: So to answer your question ... I got an e-ticket online. [[ ]] —————————-

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. Thank you. Now I’d like to ask you about your satisfaction with your journey. So what would you say you were most satisfied with today?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Well, I like the wifi on the train. It’s improved a lot. It makes it easier for me to work if I want to.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s the first time today anyone’s mentioned that. It’s good to get some positive feedback on that.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Mmm.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And, is there anything you weren’t satisfied with?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Well, normally, the trains run on time and are pretty reliable but today there was a delay [[ ]] ; the train was about 15 minutes behind schedule.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. I’ll put that down. Now I’d also like to ask about the facilities at this station. You’ve probably noticed that the whole station’s been upgraded. What are you most satisfied with?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: I think the best thing is that they’ve improved the amount of information [[ ]] about train times etc. that’s given to passengers – it’s much clearer – before there was only one board and I couldn’t always see it properly – which was frustrating.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s good. And is there anything you’re not satisfied with?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Let’s see ... I think things have generally improved a lot. The trains are much more modern and I like the new café. But one thing is that there aren’t enough places to sit down, especially on the platforms. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK – so I’ll put ‘seating’ down, shall I, as the thing you’re least satisfied with?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes, OK.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Can I ask your opinion about some of the other facilities? We’d like feedback on whether people are satisfied, dissatisfied or neither satisfied nor dissatisfied.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: What about the parking [[ ]] at the station?

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Well to be honest, I don’t really have an opinion as I never use it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: So, neither satisfied nor dissatisfied for that then.

segments.speaker: SOPHIE
segments.en: Yes, I suppose so ...

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK, and what about ...?
